Encode Residue-Centered Circular Neighborhoods

fp_circular_binary.Rd

Computes a fixed-size hashed fingerprint from residue-level Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) neighborhoods, without fitting a dictionary or training a model. fp_circular_binary() records occupied bins; fp_circular_count() sums feature occurrences, including repeated environments and collisions.

Usage

fp_circular_binary(
  glycans,
  ...,
  radius = 2L,
  n_bits = 2048L,
  na_action = "propagate"
)

fp_circular_count(
  glycans,
  ...,
  radius = 2L,
  n_bits = 2048L,
  na_action = "propagate"
)

Arguments

glycans

A glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector or a character vector in any format supported by glyparse::auto_parse(). Formats are detected automatically, as in glymotif. For explicit format selection, use the corresponding glyparse parser first. Structures must be complete: concrete residues, specified linkages, positions, substituents and reducing-end alpha/beta state. Unknown or ambiguous fields raise an error.

...

Reserved for future options. Must be empty.

radius

Maximum neighborhood radius in glycosidic edges, an integer from 0 to 10. The default 2 includes radii 0, 1 and 2.

n_bits

Number of fixed hash bins, an integer from 1 to 1048576. The default 2048 balances vector size and folding collisions; it is not optimized for a particular prediction task.

na_action

"propagate" (default) returns an all-NA vector for each missing input; "error" rejects missing inputs.

Value

A list of named integer vectors of length n_bits, preserving input length, order and names. Missing inputs produce all-NA vectors and empty input produces list(). A single residue contributes once per radius.

Details

Encoding version 1 starts with the concrete residue label (including the stereochemistry it represents), positioned substituents, the residue's own anomer/donor carbon, and a reducing-end flag. The root retains its specified alpha/beta state. Each WL round hashes the previous label with a sorted multiset of neighbor messages containing the neighbor label, full glycosidic linkage and donor/acceptor direction. This is not an atomic stereochemistry reconstruction; information absent from glyrepr labels cannot be recovered.

One occurrence per residue per radius 0 through radius is recorded, including repeated environments. A count fingerprint therefore sums to number_of_residues * (radius + 1). The iteration number distinguishes radii; equal neighborhoods at different radii are not deduplicated as in some ECFP implementations. Limited radius can miss differences in long-range layout. This is a residue-level WL design inspired by circular molecular fingerprints, not an exact implementation of atom-level Morgan/ECFP or MAP4.

Fixed hashing and collisions

Fields are UTF-8 strings prefixed by their byte lengths. Full SHA-256 digests encode WL labels and method-specific features. The first 32 bits of each final digest, interpreted big-endian, are reduced modulo n_bits to select a bin. Colliding features add their counts or share a binary bit. There is no random seed, learned vocabulary, or batch-dependent dictionary. Distinct structures can share a fingerprint because of feature loss or collisions; equality is not proof of isomorphism. Larger n_bits reduces folding collisions but does not restore missing structural information. Bin names encode method, version, radius, dimension and mode. Compare vectors only under identical settings and compatible package/dependency versions. Counts are occurrence counts, not counts of unique subgraphs. No torch runtime or model weights are used.

Complete structures

All fingerprint functions validate complete input structures. Missing inputs are distinct from unknown structure fields: empty input returns list() and missing inputs retain the full coordinate set filled with NA values. Recompute compared vectors when the model, dictionary or implementation changes.

References

Rogers and Hahn (2010). Extended-connectivity fingerprints. doi:10.1021/ci100050t . Shervashidze et al. (2011). Weisfeiler-Lehman graph kernels. https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v12/shervashidze11a.html.

See also

fp_residue_pair(), fp_motif_count(), fp_motif_binary()

Examples

x <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", "Gal(b1-3)GlcNAc(b1-")
fp <- fp_circular_binary(x)
lengths(fp)
#> [1] 2048 2048
identical(fp_circular_binary(x[1]), fp[1])
#> [1] TRUE
sum(fp_circular_count(x[1])[[1]])
#> [1] 6
